subline

Read what your friends are actually saying.

Subline puts a translation underneath any Discord message written in a language you don't read. It runs inside the Discord you already have — same app, same account, same servers. Nothing to learn, nothing to switch to.

Installing

Your computer will warn you. Here is exactly what it says, and why.

Subline isn’t code-signed yet, so your computer shows a warning the first time. It means "we haven’t paid for a certificate," not "we found a problem." Here’s how to get past it.

  1. Open the downloaded file, then drag Subline to Applications.

    Ordinary so far.

  2. Double-click Subline. macOS refuses and shows this.

    macOS says"Subline" Not Opened — Apple could not verify "Subline" is free of malware that may harm your Mac or compromise your privacy.

    Read it precisely: could not verify, not found malware. macOS is saying it has no certificate to check against, because none was bought.

  3. Open System Settings › Privacy & Security and scroll down.

    macOS says"Subline" was blocked to protect your Mac.  Open Anyway

    Click Open Anyway, then confirm with your password or Touch ID. You only do this once, for this app.

  4. Subline asks for App Management permission.

    This is the real ask, and it is the one worth thinking about. It is the right to modify another installed app — Subline needs it to add its translation file inside Discord. You can withdraw it at any time in the same Settings pane, and Subline will simply stop updating itself.

  5. That's the last of it.

    Discord closes, reopens, and translations start appearing. Nothing further is ever asked.

If you'd rather not take our word for it

The source is public and the whole change to Discord is one file. You can read it, build Subline yourself, and skip every warning above — a signed app you didn't read is not safer than an unsigned one you did.

Privacy

Where your messages go

Translation cannot happen without sending the text somewhere. Here is every place it goes, in plain terms. We would rather you decide against Subline knowing this than install it without.

WhatGoes whereKept?
Message textGoogle Translate for a Quick translation. Anthropic's API for a Careful one, if you've added a key.Not by us. We store nothing and run no server.
Who sent itNowhere. Names, avatars, server and channel names are never sent.—
Your API keyStays on your computer, in Discord's own settings storage. Sent only to Anthropic, only by you.On your machine.
Usage dataNone collected. No analytics, no crash reporting, no telemetry of any kind.—
  • off
    Direct messages are not translated unless you turn them on. Off by default, per conversation, and it stays off until you say otherwise.
  • off
    Messages already in your reading language are never sent anywhere. Detection happens on your computer first.
  • you
    You can switch translation off per channel. Nothing leaves your machine from a channel you've disabled.

The honest part

Google and Anthropic have their own terms, and once text reaches them it is governed by those, not by us. If a conversation is sensitive enough that a third party reading it would matter, turn Subline off for that channel — or don't install it. That is a real trade, and it is yours to make.
